containerDefinitions.name: work
command:
import time,signal,sys,json,hashlib
signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM,lambda *_:sys.exit(0))
print(json.dumps({'event':'started','at':time.time()}),flush=True)
while time.time()<1789610736:
 t=time.process_time()
 while time.process_time()-t<0.002: hashlib.sha256(b'stackd-bounded-workload').digest()
 time.sleep(0.2)
print(json.dumps({'event':'deadline','at':time.time()}),flush=True)

command:
import time,signal,sys,json,hashlib
signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM,lambda *_:sys.exit(0))
print(json.dumps({'event':'started','at':time.time()}),flush=True)
while time.time()<1789610736:
 t=time.process_time()
 while time.process_time()-t<0.002: hashlib.sha256(b'stackd-bounded-workload').digest()
 time.sleep(0.2)
print(json.dumps({'event':'deadline','at':time.time()}),flush=True)

import time,signal,sys,json,hashlib
signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM,lambda *_:sys.exit(0))
print(json.dumps({'event':'started','at':time.time()}),flush=True)
while time.time()<1789610736:
 t=time.process_time()
 while time.process_time()-t<0.002: hashlib.sha256(b'stackd-bounded-workload').digest()
 time.sleep(0.2)
print(json.dumps({'event':'deadline','at':time.time()}),flush=True)

experiment.targetTrackingPath: tightly controlled custom metric, not CPU; publisher adjusts offered units by observed running capacity

controllerHandoff.reason: Anchor bounded live-workload controller to first native task startedAt rather than pre-schedule setup time. Same resources and policies; no deployment or metric backdating.

experiment.manualStatePath: Real SetAlarmState API with explicit test StateReasonData, never claimed to be emitted metric observations. Separate never-published metric alarm used same real StepScaling ARN; deleted before target-tracking phase.

liveWorkloadEvidence.note: Task stoppedAt includes later network/deprovisioning; executionStoppedAt bounds actual workload execution. All native fields retained.

findings.behavior: Scheduled suspension skips a passed one-time action; resumption did not replay it in the captured immediate read. A subsequent scheduled action changed target min/max from0/2 to1/2 and actual ECS capacity0→1.

Real high-resolution CloudWatch step alarm entered ALARM while dynamic scale-out was suspended; actual capacity remained1. After resume the same alarm, without a new state transition, drove PercentChangeInCapacity +10 at running1 to desired/running2. Configured cooldown120; subsequent diagnostic AlreadyAtDesiredCapacity reported CurrentCapacity2.

Target tracking used the explicitly controlled custom metric OfferedUnitsPerTask, not CPU. Publisher divided offered units by observed running capacity. Native GetMetricStatistics confirms high100 and subsequent low1 datapoints. Real target tracking scaled running capacity1→2.
findings.scope: Metric values were deliberate experiment inputs; all API results, alarms, task transitions and provider errors are native.

findings.behavior: For target50 native managed High alarm has Period60/EvaluationPeriods3/GreaterThanThreshold50; Low has Period60/EvaluationPeriods15/LessThanThreshold45. DatapointsToAlarm and TreatMissingData were absent, not synthesized. Both managed AlarmActions append :createdBy/<uuid> to the policy ARN.

Target-tracking High remained ALARM01:47:59Z–01:50:59Z. Scale-out activity began01:47:59.264Z; separate AlreadyAtMaxCapacity/MaxCapacity2 activity at01:49:59.225Z occurred without a new alarm state transition, proving subsequent scaling evaluation at saturation. CloudWatch history retained only the initial Action entry, not a per-retry delivery log.
findings.intervalLimit: Observed distinct attempts are119.961 seconds apart; this does not establish every delivery interval. Official documentation specifies repeated Auto Scaling alarm actions once per minute.

findings.behavior: SetAlarmState API succeeded without StateReasonData but Action history failed with StateReasonData must be provided. PascalCase example fields failed with Metric data points must be provided. Stale native lowercase data failed with a scaling-deemed-unsafe parsing/outdated-timestamp message. Fresh lowercase reason data caused Action Succeeded for the real AAS policy ARN.
findings.limit: The manually triggered action ran at maximum capacity; immediate activity lookup did not contain a distinct manual-alarm activity, so this proves successful policy action invocation, not a manual capacity increase.

findings.behavior: CloudTrail actual desired-count changes used the ECS Application Auto Scaling service-linked role with AutoScaling-UpdateDesiredCapacity and invokedBy ecs.application-autoscaling.amazonaws.com. Initial managed PutMetricAlarm calls instead used the original IAMUser with invokedBy application-autoscaling.amazonaws.com. Managed DeleteAlarms during policy deletion used the service-linked role with AutoScaling-ManageAlarms.
Both AWSServiceRoleForECS and AWSServiceRoleForApplicationAutoScaling_ECSService pre-existed. Neither global role was created or deleted by this capture.

uncertainties: CloudTrail lookup is bounded to one page per operation after cleanup; delivery lag/pagination means missing records are not evidence of absence.

Actual target-tracking scale-in was NOT observed. Low phase began01:48:48.605590Z; native01:48 metric average62.75 was not below45, subsequent one-minute averages were1. The managed Low alarm remained OK through the last completed read before the02:04:28Z watchdog. Managed policy/alarms were then deleted and tasks stopped. No backdated metrics or managed alarm edits were used to manufacture scale-in evidence.

Step cooldown enforcement was not isolated from desired-count/max-capacity saturation under the hard maximum2. Cooldown120 was configured, but no distinct cooldown-specific blocking reason was observed; do not generalize the diagnostic AlreadyAtDesiredCapacity into proof of a cooldown formula.

A controller deadline interrupted one in-flight DescribeAlarms call; no response for that interrupted request is fabricated. The TimeoutError and controller handoff are retained. The actual workload execution interval was1475.092 seconds, below1500 seconds; provider task deprovisioning completed later.

The task definition remains a non-runnable DELETE_IN_PROGRESS native metadata tombstone after accepted DeleteTaskDefinitions. Final ListTaskDefinitions statusACTIVE is empty. ECS service and cluster are INACTIVE; CloudWatch retains historical custom metric datapoints because no DeleteMetric API exists.

cleanup.customMetricRetention: CloudWatch has no DeleteMetric API; publishing stopped, historical datapoints expire by native retention.
cleanup.verificationScope: All billable/active owned resources removed; native INACTIVE ECS service/cluster, STOPPED exit0 tasks, DELETE_IN_PROGRESS task-definition tombstone, no active task definitions, targets/policies/schedules/alarms/logs/execution role/network. Historical metrics and native tombstones retain provider lifecycle semantics.
